subject: Train 2, F7 passenger consist, nearest placed train to the working iron ore mine (1.54 km at start), with the saved follow-camera framing.
finding: Origin rebasing moved the listener and train visuals but only reset audio velocity history. Emitters remained at their old coordinates until the next train-audio update. The independent spatial mixer could observe a false 512 m separation and silence the mix for one 512-sample block.
evidence: Baseline: two exact 512-sample (10.667 ms) stereo silence gaps at master times 36.896 and 48.330667 seconds, immediately following measured rebases at 36.880601 and 48.313218 seconds.
Both gaps are present in the Windows WASAPI loopback recording about 27 ms later, confirming game-generated discontinuities rather than a capture-only artifact.
The associated frames lasted 14.79 and 14.18 ms and had zero terrain uploads. Peak master amplitude was 0.108, far below clipping, and capture discarded zero frames.
Control without origin rebasing: zero silence gaps with 335 terrain uploads still occurring during the 55-second recording.
Fixed run: zero gaps in either master or Windows output across 75 seconds, six measured origin shifts and 402 terrain uploads.
fix: TrainAudio.Rebase immediately translates every engine/wheel/curve emitter, steam-chuff container and horn, plus stored listener/source positions. Playback state and Doppler history survive the rebase; streams are not restarted.
validation: Godot --suite=train-audio: PASS, including immediate emitter relocation and preservation of playing state/pitch
Native GPU fixed follow capture: PASS
capture: 48 kHz stereo float32 master-bus WAV and concurrent WASAPI default-output loopback; native Compatibility OpenGL at 1280x800 on RX 6600. No microphone capture. The original save is untouched; all runs use its copy.
limitations: Whole output-endpoint recording can include unrelated desktop audio. The separate master-bus recording contains only this game.
Loopback wall-clock alignment is approximate due to device buffering; the master sample clock and per-frame origin events provide the primary correlation.
This verifies the reproduced origin-shift dropouts, not the absence of every possible audible artifact. Audio-only random wheel detuning makes recordings non-identical.
